classification.difficultyReason: Use shaded models to express fractions in equal-sized cells; later parts require choosing and adding subdivisions before subtracting and simplifying, with earlier completed subdivisions providing a model.

content.prompt: Add and subtract these fractions using the visual models.

spec.description: Two rows of paired equal-sized squares: original fifths and quarters above equivalent twentieths.
spec.mathematics: Two fifths equals eight twentieths; one quarter equals five twentieths.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied shaded models remain visible; numerical responses are omitted.

answer.worked:
The models show $8$ shaded twentieths and $5$ shaded twentieths.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{8}{20}+\frac{5}{20}\\&=\frac{13}{20}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Original thirds and sevenths above two three-by-seven grids.
spec.mathematics: Two thirds equals fourteen twenty-firsts; one seventh equals three twenty-firsts.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied models visible; numerical answers absent.

answer.worked:
The models show $14$ shaded twenty-firsts and $3$ shaded twenty-firsts.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{7}&=\frac{14}{21}+\frac{3}{21}\\&=\frac{17}{21}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Original fifths and thirds above paired five-by-three grids; lower-left erroneous seven-column subdivision corrected.
spec.mathematics: Three fifths and one third are supplied; equivalent models shade nine fifteenths and five fifteenths.
spec.answerVisibility: Shaded fractional quantities visible; numerical responses absent.

answer.worked:
The equal-sized cells represent fifteenths. Subtract 5 shaded cells from 9.
$$\begin{align*}\frac35-\frac13&=\frac9{15}-\frac5{15}\\&=\frac4{15}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Both rows show four shaded fifths and two shaded quarters. Lower figures retain space for student subdivisions.
spec.mathematics: The same whole is partitioned into fifths on the left and quarters on the right.
spec.answerVisibility: Common-denominator subdivisions and numerical answers are not supplied.

answer.worked:
Subdivide both lower models into $20$ equal cells: $16$ are shaded on the left and $10$ on the right.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{5}-\frac{2}{4}&=\frac{16}{20}-\frac{10}{20}\\&=\frac{6}{20}\\&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Both models completed as five-by-four grids.
spec.mathematics: Sixteen twentieths minus ten twentieths leaves six twentieths.

spec.description: Both rows show four shaded fifths and four shaded sixths. Lower figures remain available for subdivisions.
spec.mathematics: Starting quantity four fifths; subtracted quantity four sixths.
spec.answerVisibility: Student subdivisions and numerical responses absent.

answer.worked:
Subdivide both lower models into $30$ equal cells: $24$ are shaded on the left and $20$ on the right.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{5}-\frac{4}{6}&=\frac{24}{30}-\frac{20}{30}\\&=\frac{4}{30}\\&=\frac{2}{15}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Both models completed as five-by-six grids.
spec.mathematics: Twenty-four thirtieths minus twenty thirtieths leaves four thirtieths.

spec.description: Both rows show four shaded fifths and one shaded half. Lower figures remain available for subdivisions.
spec.mathematics: Starting quantity four fifths; subtracted quantity one half.
spec.answerVisibility: Student subdivisions and numerical responses absent.

answer.worked:
Subdivide both lower models into $10$ equal cells: $8$ are shaded on the left and $5$ on the right.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{8}{10}-\frac{5}{10}\\&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$
